points: Q3 fee revenue growth vs the Q2 pace that reports suggest was 4.7% will reveal whether Exchange premium growth is reaccelerating or fading into 2027; a beat that pushes 90-day revenue revisions above +0.5% would create a long, while a miss that drives them below -0.5% would create a short.

The print will show whether commission costs, which reports suggest surged in Q2, are growing faster or slower than fee revenue; a compressing commission ratio supports a long, and another surge supports a short.
Q3 underwriting margin will reveal whether the Q2 turnaround is durable; continued improvement supports a long, and renewed deterioration supports a short.

Management's pricing and retention commentary will show whether Erie is maintaining rate discipline into the 2027 renewal season; holding discipline supports a long, while broad rate cuts to chase growth support a short.

Peer prints from GSHD, MRSH, RYAN and AJG around ERIE's report will provide a sector read-through on broker fee growth and pricing; stronger guidance supports a long, and cuts or soft outlook support a short.
With FY1/FY2 consensus unavailable and the Insurance Brokers theme cold/flat, the trade will be decided by whether Q3 results shift the 90-day revenue estimate revision out of the neutral band.
watch: Q3 fee revenue growth vs Q2's reported/suggested 4.7%: faster supports long, slower supports short.
Commission expense growth relative to fee revenue: slower supports long, faster supports short.
Underwriting margin trend: improvement supports long, deterioration supports short.
90-day revenue estimate revision (rev90): above +0.5% establishes long, below -0.5% establishes short.
